analysis.reason: This study models the Galactic population of dormant neutron star binaries and forecasts Gaia DR4/DR5 astrometric yields, providing quantitative constraints on core-collapse supernova engines, natal kicks, and dense matter equations of state.
analysis.result: Under the realistic selection function gaiamock, Gaia is predicted to detect $\sim 100\text{--}110$ and $\sim 300\text{--}380$ dormant neutron star--luminous companion (NS--LC) binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively. In the intrinsic population, $\sim 94\%$ of surviving detached systems survive through common envelope (CE) evolution ($P_{\rm orb} \le 10\,\mathrm{yr}$). The observed NS mass distribution peaks sharply at $1.2\text{--}1.3\,M_\odot$ driven by low-kick ($\sigma = 20\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) electron-capture supernovae (ECSN), while delayed core-collapse supernova (CCSN) fallback produces massive NSs exceeding $M_{\rm NS} > 2.5\,M_\odot$ in $\sim 1\%$ of systems. Pulsar spin-down and magnetic field decay follow $\dot{P}_{\rm spin} = K \frac{B^2}{P_{\rm spin}}$ ($K = 9.87 \times 10^{-48}\,\mathrm{yr\,G^{-2}}$), death line $B/P_{\rm spin}^2 = 0.17 \times 10^{12}\,\mathrm{G\,s^{-2}}$, and accretion-induced burial $B = \frac{B_0}{1 + \Delta M / (10^{-6}\,M_\odot)} \exp\left(-\frac{T - t_{\rm acc}}{\tau}\right)$ with $\tau = 3\,\mathrm{Gyr}$.
analysis.problem: Quantifying the Galactic population of dormant neutron stars in detached binaries with luminous companions (NS--LC) detectable via astrometric orbital wobbles in Gaia DR4 and DR5, and testing whether their yields and orbital parameters can break degeneracies between core-collapse supernova explosion models (rapid vs. delayed), natal kicks ($\sigma = 265\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ vs. $20\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$), and common envelope evolution.
analysis.method: Binary population synthesis using COSMIC initialized with a Kroupa IMF ($3 < m_{\rm pri}/M_\odot < 60$), flat mass ratios ($q = m_{\rm sec}/m_{\rm pri}$), thermal eccentricities, and log-flat semi-major axes up to $10^5\,R_\odot$. Spatial distribution and star formation histories are drawn from the FIRE-2 m12i Milky Way simulation ($10^{-4} \le Z \le 0.03$). Supernova prescriptions incorporate rapid and delayed core-collapse models (maximum $M_{\rm NS} = 3\,M_\odot$), ECSN ($M_{\rm ZAMS} \sim 8\text{--}10\,M_\odot$, $M_{\rm Ch} \approx 1.38\,M_\odot$), and accretion-induced collapse (AIC), followed by synthetic observation through CCB22 and gaiamock astrometric selection functions.
assumptions: The Milky Way binary population follows star formation and metallicity distributions from the FIRE-2 m12i simulation evaluated across 100 Galactic realizations.
limits: The isolated binary evolution models produce no detached millisecond pulsars (MSPs) with main-sequence companions, in contrast to 29 known field radio MSPs in tight orbits from the ATNF pulsar catalog.
citation_leads: II.4 Synthetic galactic population: “We create 100 Galactic realisations for the NS–LC binary population.”
III.2 Gaia observable NS–LC Population: “The predicted numbers of detectable NS–LC binaries depend only weakly on the adopted SN prescription.”
V Conclusions: “predict $\sim 100$–$110$ and $\sim 300$–$380$ detectable NS–LC binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively”
IV Comparison with Known Pulsars in the ATNF Pulsar catalog: “Our models thus produce no detached MSPs with MS companions”
analysis.research_progress: Shows that extended baseline observations from Gaia DR3 (34 months) to DR4 (66 months) will increase detectable NS--LC binaries by two orders of magnitude. Demonstrates that while gaiamock selection washes out intrinsic rapid vs. delayed SN mass differences by favoring low-kick ECSN systems, a DR4 detection exceeding $\sim 100$ systems will directly confirm non-isolated dynamical formation channels in clusters or triples.

Filled plus signs and triangles show the simulated pulsars in detached NS – MS binaries and the simulated MSPs in detached NS – PMS binaries, respectively, in the intrinsic population for the rapid SN model. Circles and the star show the ATNF pulsars with MS companions, including MSPs, in the MW field and in the SMC (PSR J0045 $-$ 7319), respectively; pulsars in globular clusters are excluded. The color of each symbol indicates the ${{P_{\rm{orb}}}}$ of the binary, shown on a logarithmic scale in the color bar. The dashed line shows the pulsar death line, $B/P_{\rm spin}^{2}=0.17\times 10^{12}\,{\rm G\,s^{-2}}$. The corresponding figure for the delayed SN model is shown in Figure A5 in the Appendix.
figures.label: Fig. 8

figures.caption: Figure 7: Orbital period–eccentricity distribution of Gaia -detectable NS – LC binaries (MS and PMS companions combined) for the rapid SN model, combining all 100 Galactic realizations. Left and right panels show binaries detectable with the CCB22 and gaiamock selection functions, respectively. Green circles and red plus signs denote DR5 and DR4 detections, respectively. analysis.reason: The paper develops a unified Poynting-flux-dominated jet model connecting fast X-ray transients (FXTs) to gamma-ray bursts via premature magnetic dissipation when the jet satisfies the causal condition $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma < 1$.
analysis.result: Premature kink instability dissipates Poynting flux at stellar breakout radius $R_* \sim 10^{11}\,\mathrm{cm}$ with Lorentz factor $\Gamma \sim 20$, yielding rapid thermalization where mean comoving photon energy $\langle E' \rangle \sim 2.7 k_{\rm B} [L_{\rm iso}/(4\pi R_*^2 \Gamma^2 a c)]^{1/4} \sim 0.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ escapes as soft X-rays with thermalization timescale $\tau_{\rm th} \sim N_{\rm th} R_* / (\ell' c)$, minimum variability timescale $\Delta t_{\rm var} \simeq (1+z) R_{\rm ph} \theta_{\rm J}^2 / (2c) \sim 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{s}$, and no jet breaks because $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma < 1$ holds throughout.
analysis.problem: Explaining the physical nature of fast X-ray transients (FXTs) associated with type Ic-BL supernovae that exhibit soft thermal X-ray spectra, low peak energies, long deceleration times, and an absence of geometric jet breaks.
analysis.method: Modeling Blandford–Znajek driven Poynting-flux-dominated jets with initial magnetization $\sigma_0 \gg 1$ accelerating via ideal MHD magnetic pressure gradient as $\Gamma(R) = \sigma_0^{3/2}(R/R_{\rm sat})^{1/3}$, where global kink instability triggers premature dissipation at $R_*$ if $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R_*) < 1$.
assumptions: The relativistic jet is Poynting-flux dominated with initial magnetization $\sigma_0 \equiv \dot{E}_{\rm Poynting}/\dot{E}_{\rm kinetic} \gg 1$ accelerating as $\Gamma(R) \propto R^{1/3}$ before saturation.
limits: Global kink instability requires the entire jet cross-section to remain causally connected under $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R) < 1$.
citation_leads: II The model: “if the jet opening angle $\theta_{\rm J}$ satisfies $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R)<1”
III Confronting observations: “$\theta_{J}\Gamma<1$ holds at all times, so no jet break is expected regardless of the opening angle.”
References: “A fast X-ray transient from a weak relativistic jet associated with a type Ic-BL supernova.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that a critical magnetization threshold $\sigma_0 \approx 45$ divides premature-dissipated FXTs ($\sigma_0 \lesssim 45$, $\Gamma \lesssim 50$) from standard GRBs ($\sigma_0 > 45$, $\Gamma > 100$), naturally reproducing FXT thermal spectra and lack of jet breaks within relativistic jet physics.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic of the jet evolution scenario. A Poynting-flux-dominated jet is launched from the central engine and propagates through the progenitor envelope. Kink instability may develops in the magnetically dominated flow, triggering premature magnetic dissipation at low Lorentz factor, producing the fast X-ray transient (FXT). In the sketch, we also plot the case when the premature dissipation is absence, the jet continues accelerating to ultra-relativistic Lorentz factor and produces a classical gamma-ray burst (GRB) via dissipation at larger radii.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: Schematic of the unified jet evolution scenario: a Poynting-flux-dominated jet launched from the central engine either suffers kink instability triggering premature magnetic dissipation at low Lorentz factor ($\\Gamma \\lesssim 50$) inside the envelope to produce a fast X-ray transient (FXT), or avoids premature dissipation to accelerate to ultra-relativistic velocities ($\\Gamma > 100$) and dissipate at larger radii ($\\sim 10^{15}\\text{ cm}$) as a classical gamma-ray burst (GRB).

figures.caption: Figure 2: Model prediction for $\Gamma(R_{\rm dis})$ (solid black, left axis) and $\ell^{\prime}$ (dashed, right axis, for $L=10^{48}$ erg s -1 ) as functions of $\sigma_{0}$. Red shading: FXT regime ($\sigma_{0} 45$, dissipation beyond $R_{*}$). The vertical segment at $\sigma_{0}=45$ connects the two branches. Observed events are marked at their inferred $\sigma_{0}$: EP241113a ($\Gamma\approx 20$; Dai et al. 2026) and EP240414a ($\Gamma\approx 6.5$, from the inner cocoon constraint of Zheng et al. 2025) have $\Gamma$ measurements in the literature; events marked with ∗ (EP250108a, XRF 241001A) lack a precise $\Gamma$ measurement and are shown at illustrative $\sigma_{0}$ values. EP240801a ∗ is placed at the FXT/GRB boundary ($\sigma_{0}=45$) by model construction; its $\Gamma$ is not independently constrained by observations.
figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.physical_core: Theoretical evolution curves for Lorentz factor $\\Gamma(R_{\\rm dis})$ and compactness parameter $\\ell^{\\prime}$ as functions of initial magnetization $\\sigma_{0}$, delineating the boundary at $\\sigma_{0} = 45$ between the FXT regime (premature dissipation inside $R_{*}$) and the standard GRB regime (dissipation beyond $R_{*}$), with observational constraints from well-studied FXTs (e.g., EP241113a, EP240414a, and EP240801a) placed along the transition.

analysis.reason: The paper provides upper limits on the isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux at $100\ \mathrm{TeV}$ to $10\ \mathrm{PeV}$ using the Carpet-3 EAS array at Baksan Neutrino Observatory, providing direct constraints on the origin of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, UHECR propagation, and exotic physics.
analysis.result: Carpet-3 reports 90% CL upper limits on the isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux under an assumed $E^{-2}$ power-law spectrum over $100\ \mathrm{TeV} - 10\ \mathrm{PeV}$: the integral upper limit is $\Phi_{\gamma} < 3.2\times 10^{-13}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-2}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}\ \mathrm{sr}^{-1}$ at $\log_{10}(E_{\mathrm{min}}/\mathrm{eV}) = 14.0$ (efficiency $\varepsilon_{\gamma}=0.004$) and reaches $\Phi_{\gamma} < 2.8\times 10^{-14}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-2}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}\ \mathrm{sr}^{-1}$ at $\log_{10}(E_{\mathrm{min}}/\mathrm{eV}) = 15.75$ ($\varepsilon_{\gamma}=0.84$). An excess of photon candidate events above expected background is observed below $1\ \mathrm{PeV}$ (e.g., 55 candidates vs 8 expected at $\log_{10}(E/\mathrm{eV}) = 14.375$).
analysis.problem: Disentangling an isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux from intense hadronic cosmic-ray background in EAS observations without off-source control regions, while eliminating systematic domain shift between Monte Carlo simulations and experimental detector responses.
analysis.method: A neural network classifier combining a 2D convolutional network for energy deposition in the 400-scintillator center array and a fully connected network for reconstructed parameters ($N_e$, shower age $s$, and muon number $n_\mu^{410}$), optimized via unsupervised domain adaptation with a gradient reversal layer ($-\lambda$) to suppress simulation-experiment discrepancy, determining 90% CL flux limits via Feldman-Cousins statistics maximizing $\alpha = \varepsilon(\xi_0) / N_{\mathrm{bkg}}^{90}(\xi_0)$ over effective exposure $\mathcal{E}(E) = T \int_\Omega A_{\mathrm{eff}}(E, \theta, \phi)\, \mathrm{d}\Omega$.
limits: Converting the candidate event excess below $1\ \mathrm{PeV}$ into a definitive gamma-ray flux measurement is deferred to future work

III.2 Domain adaptation: “To mitigate this and make network predictions more reliable, we use domain adaptation with gradient reversal”
V Conclusions: “We observe an excess of photon candidate events below 1 PeV above the expected background.”
V Conclusions: “converting this excess into a gamma-ray flux measurement requires further dedicated analysis”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that unsupervised domain adaptation with gradient reversal suppresses the KL divergence between experimental EAS observables and simulations by a factor of $\sim 15$, yielding competitive PeV-scale diffuse gamma-ray constraints while identifying tentative sub-PeV candidate excesses.

analysis.reason: This paper presents an unprecedented, continuously monitored common envelope evolution event and stellar merger in M31 (AT 2025abao), directly probing circumstellar material (CSM) interaction and plateau emission mechanisms relevant to shock interaction and plateau studies in transients.
analysis.result: The progenitor is identified as an early AGB star ($M_1 \approx 7\,M_\odot$, $R_{\rm eff} \approx 350\,R_\odot$, $L \approx 1.8 \times 10^4\,L_\odot$, $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-5}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr^{-1}}$) with a low-mass companion ($M_2 \approx 0.7\,M_\odot$, mass ratio $q=0.10_{-0.08}^{+0.10}$). The 7-year precursor brightening ($L_{\rm drag} \approx 3 \times 10^{38}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$) was driven by frictional drag in the primary's convective envelope, transitioning to a dynamic plunge and luminous red nova eruption with ejecta kinetic energy $KE_{\rm ej} \sim 10^{48}\,{\rm erg}$ and unbound mass $\sim 0.2\text{--}0.4\,M_\odot$, whose optical plateau is powered by momentum-conserving shock interaction with equatorial CSM having $\rho(r) \propto r^{-2}$.

analysis.reason: The paper develops a parameter-free, high-order smoothness indicator for AMR in Newtonian, SRMHD, and GRMHD simulations, demonstrating robust tracking of relativistic blast waves and black hole accretion flows with significant speedups.
analysis.result: The indicator accurately captures discontinuities and shear layers across tests: in Kelvin–Helmholtz instability tests with $\Gamma=5/3$ and effective resolution $2048^{2}$, it speeds up computation by $1.45\times$; in SRMHD magnetic rotor tests, it achieves a $3.4\times$ reduction in MeshBlock-cycles and $2.8\times$ wall-clock speedup; in GRMHD MAD simulations around Kerr black holes ($a/M_{\rm BH}=0.9, \phi_{\rm BH} = \Phi_{\rm BH}/\sqrt{\dot{M}} \gtrsim 15$), it successfully resolves jet launching, though computational savings diminish when the region $r \le 100r_g$ becomes fully turbulent.
analysis.problem: High computational cost and lack of problem-independent, robust error indicators for adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) in multi-dimensional Newtonian, SRMHD, and GRMHD simulations.
analysis.method: Adapted from spectral modal falloff indicators, the scheme calculates the 4th-order undivided finite difference $\Delta^{(4)}u = u_{i+2}-4u_{i+1}+6u_{i}-4u_{i-1}+u_{i-2}$ over a symmetric 5-point stencil to obtain the oscillation measure $e_i = |\Delta^{(4)}u/u_i|$, applying fixed thresholds $4^{-2}=0.0625$ for refinement and $4^{-3}=0.015625$ for coarsening across conserved variables $(D, M^j, E, B^j)$ in AthenaK.
assumptions: Monitored physical fields are sufficiently smooth away from true discontinuities such that high-order polynomial modal coefficients decay rapidly.
limits: AMR computational savings diminish once turbulence fills the entire domain of interest (such as fully developed post-eruption MAD states at $r \le 100r_g$), and initial discontinuities require pre-refinement to prevent staircasing artifacts.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first binary population synthesis coupled with time-dependent synchrotron nebular models for hyper-Eddington mass-transfer systems, directly constraining persistent radio source (PRS) counterparts to repeating FRBs, relativistic jet inflation, and radio transient surveys.
analysis.result: The local volumetric birth rate of hyper-Eddington mass-transfer binaries is $\mathcal{R} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ spanning $\dot{m} \sim 10^{2\text{--}7}$ and accretion timescales $t_{\rm acc} \sim 10^{0\text{--}6}\,\mathrm{yr}$. The systems launch mildly relativistic jets ($v_{\rm j} \sim 0.1\text{--}0.3c$) and disk winds ($v_{\rm w} \sim 0.03c$) inflating long-lived synchrotron hypernebulae with peak radio luminosities $L_{\nu,\rm peak} \sim 10^{28}\text{--}10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$ at $\sim 1\text{--}3\,\mathrm{GHz}$, overlapping with FRB-associated PRSs and yielding $\sim 10^{2\text{--}5}$ detectable steady sources in VLASS.
analysis.problem: Distinguishing unresolved synchrotron hypernebulae driven by rare, energetic hyper-Eddington binary mass transfer from other populations of unresolved synchrotron sources (such as AGNs, SNRs, and GRB afterglows) in modern wide-field radio surveys.
analysis.method: Coupled COMPAS binary population synthesis (v02.35.03) with a semi-analytic synchrotron hypernebula model. For stable RLOF, the mass-transfer rate is set by donor envelope thermal timescale $\dot{M} = \dot{M}_{\rm th} = M_{\rm d,env}/\tau_{\rm KH} = R_{\rm d}L_{\rm d}/(G M_{\rm d})$ with duration $t_{\rm acc} = \tau_{\rm KH}$, whereas unstable common-envelope evolution incorporates pre-dynamical accretion $\dot{M} = f_{\rm acc}\Delta M_{\rm CE}/(100 P_{\rm orb})$. analysis.reason: This paper provides valuable observational and theoretical constraints on neutron star crustal heating mechanisms by utilizing carbon burning instability to break the degeneracy between shallow and deep heating in KS 1731-260, offering key insights for compact object high-energy thermal evolution.
analysis.result: Enforcing the local carbon ignition instability criterion $(\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm C}}{\partial T})_P \ge (\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm cool}}{\partial T})_P$ breaks the degeneracy of quiescent cooling fits and strongly favors shallow heating overlapping the carbon fuel layer at column depth $y_* = 0.630\times 10^{12}\text{ g cm}^{-2}$. Deeper heating ($\log_{10}P = 27\text{--}28\text{ dyn cm}^{-2}$) requires nearly twice the heating strength ($q_a = 4.00\text{ MeV nucleon}^{-1}$ vs. $2.19\text{ MeV nucleon}^{-1}$ for shallow heating under CF88 rates), causing severe quiescent spectral residuals ($\Delta W \simeq 352$ vs. $\Delta W \simeq 39$) and overpredicting $2\text{--}3\text{ keV}$ counts by a factor of $\sim 5$. For the superburst decay at $d = 4.5\text{ kpc}$, depth-dependent energy deposition $e_{\rm b}(y) \propto (y/y_{\rm h})^{1/4}$ with $y_{\rm h} = 6.62\times 10^{11}\text{ g cm}^{-2}$ and total burst energy $\mathcal{E}_{\rm b} = 2.19\times 10^{42}\text{ erg}$ (residual sum 10.2) reproduces early cooling significantly better than uniform deposition (residual sum 26.6).

analysis.problem: Quiescent cooling models of accreting neutron star crusts suffer from an intrinsic degeneracy where shallow heating overlapping the fuel layer and deep heating beneath it produce nearly identical surface cooling curves by adjusting heating strength $q_a$ and core temperature $T_{\rm c}$, leaving the true physical depth and origin of shallow accretion heating unconstrained.
analysis.method: Thermal evolution is simulated with the dStar code for a neutron star ($M = 1.4\,M_\odot$, $R = 10\text{ km}$, $d = 4.5\text{ kpc}$) under RXTE/ASM reconstructed accretion rate history $\dot{M}(t)$. The model applies local carbon instability criteria $(\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm C}}{\partial T})_P \ge (\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm cool}}{\partial T})_P$ with local heating rate $\epsilon_a = \frac{\dot{M}Q_a}{M_a m_u}$, conduction cooling $\epsilon_{\rm cool} = 0.17\frac{K\rho T}{y^2}$, thermal conductivity $K = \frac{\pi^2 c^2 k_{\rm B}^2 T n_e}{3\mu_e \nu_{ei}}$, advective carbon burial/consumption $\frac{dy}{dt}$, and burst energy deposition $e_{\rm b}(y) \propto (y/y_{\rm h})^\beta$ (with $\beta = 0$ or $1/4$), followed by joint spectral fitting across 10 Chandra quiescent epochs ($0.5\text{--}7\text{ keV}$) via Nelder–Mead optimization.
assumptions: The carbon mass fraction in the ignition layer is assumed to be $X_{\rm C} = 0.20$ yielding a nuclear energy release of $\approx 2\times 10^{17}\text{ erg g}^{-1}$.
limits: Conductive cooling models predict superburst decay light curves that remain broader than observed (early flux is underpredicted and late tail is overpredicted by a factor of $\sim 3$ even when accounting for $^{23}{\rm Na}$–$^{23}{\rm Ne}$ Urca shell neutrino losses).

analysis.reason: This paper uses ASKAP POSSUM broadband polarization observations to probe statistical depolarization and Faraday dispersion across the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). It provides valuable empirical constraints on the turbulent magneto-ionic medium and thermal electron density scaling in dwarf irregular galaxies, relevant to intervening sightlines and propagation effects of extragalactic transients.
analysis.result: The fraction of polarized sources is significantly suppressed on-SMC ($f_{\mathrm{pol,on}} = 0.227 \pm 0.021$) compared to off-SMC ($f_{\mathrm{pol,off}} = 0.360 \pm 0.015$), accompanied by an enhanced Faraday depth dispersion $\Sigma_{\phi_{\mathrm{peak}}} = 74 \pm 9\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}}$. Modeling external Faraday dispersion with Burn's law gives $\sigma_\phi = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ with $k = 0.32$, implying a tangled random magnetic field strength $B_r = (1.0 \pm 0.2)\,(l_0/0.5\ \mathrm{pc})^{-1/2}\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ ($B_r \approx 0.3\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ at the beam scale $\sim 6\ \mathrm{pc}$).
analysis.problem: Determining whether depolarization of background radio sources in the SMC is driven by small-scale thermal electron density fluctuations or turbulent random magnetic fields, and assessing whether small-scale Faraday dispersion matches extrapolations of the large-scale RM power spectrum.
analysis.method: Subtracted SMC diffuse emission, performed RM synthesis and Stokes $QU$-fitting on POSSUM Pilot II data ($800-1088\ \mathrm{MHz}$), and modeled external Faraday dispersion $\sigma_\phi = 0.812\,n_e\,B_\parallel\,\sqrt{l_0\,L} = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ combined with $\mathrm{H}\alpha$-derived emission measure $\left(\frac{\mathrm{EM}}{\mathrm{cm^{-6}\ pc}}\right) \approx 2.75 \left(\frac{I_{\mathrm{H}\alpha,\mathrm{corr}}}{\mathrm{R}}\right) \left(\frac{T_e}{10^4\ \mathrm{K}}\right)^{0.942}$.
assumptions: Thermal electron density $n_e$ is assumed to be approximately constant across small scales, attributing Faraday dispersion primarily to random magnetic field fluctuations.
limits: Faraday complexity and multi-component structures are predominantly intrinsic to background sources or foreground Milky Way emission rather than SMC magneto-ionic turbulence.

analysis.reason: The paper uses an unseen-species statistical framework on CHIME/FRB repeaters to demonstrate that repeating FRB sources cease activity within a few years rather than emitting steadily, placing strict demographic constraints on young magnetar engines.
analysis.result: Steady Poisson activity is decisively ruled out ($p < 10^{-4}$, with no mock catalog out of 10,000 yielding $S \le 0.530$). The gap ratio $R(\Delta) = n^{\rm obs}/n^{\rm pred} \approx 1$ at $\Delta \lesssim 60\,\mathrm{d}$ decreases by half within one year. Fitting extinction models yields a characteristic lifetime $\tau = 2.9^{+1.1}_{-0.9}\,\mathrm{yr}$ (single lifetime), an active duration $T_{\rm on} = 800^{+400}_{-400}\,\mathrm{days}$ with duty cycle $d = 0.3^{+0.05}_{-0.2}$ (on/off model), or short-lifetime $\tau_s = 500^{+300}_{-200}\,\mathrm{days}$ with long-lived fraction $\eta = 0.3^{+0.2}_{-0.1}$ (mixture model). The implied birth rate satisfies $\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm birth}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm mag}} \sim 0.1 \left(\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm FRB}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm CCSN}}\right) \left(\frac{0.1}{f_{\rm b}}\right) \left(\frac{0.4}{f_{\rm mag}}\right) \left(\frac{100\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}}{\bar{r}}\right)$, indicating only $\sim 10\%$ of newborn magnetars need to be active repeaters.
analysis.reading_entry: IV The activity is not steady
analysis.problem: Whether repeating FRBs maintain steady Poisson activity over multi-year baselines, and what their true active lifetime is across the source population without being biased by rare hyperactive sources.
analysis.method: Employs Robbins' formula for unseen species estimation, where the burst yield in window $B$ ($T_B$) is predicted from detections $N_{k+1}$ in window $A$ ($T_A$) via $n_k^{\rm pred} = (k+1) N_{k+1} (T_B/T_A)$ independent of rate distribution $f(r)$. Evaluates the gap statistic $R(\Delta) = n^{\rm obs}/n^{\rm pred}$ using sliding windows ($W = 180\,\mathrm{d}$, step $30\,\mathrm{d}$, $k \le 3$), and derives the exposure ratio $t = T_B/T_A$ self-consistently from new source counts via the Good–Toulmin estimator $N_{\rm new} = \sum_{k\ge 1} (-1)^{k+1} t^k N_k$.

analysis.research_progress: Rules out steady Poisson repeating FRB populations ($p < 10^{-4}$) on a multi-year baseline and reveals that repeating activity declines on a timescale of $\tau \approx 1\text{--}3\,\mathrm{yr}$, implying that many observed one-off FRBs are dormant repeaters.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the discovery and multiwavelength follow-up of WFST0533buha (Bi'an), a fast blue ultraluminous transient (FBUT/LFBOT) candidate that exhibits unusually red blue/NUV colors and rapid photometric evolution, expanding the observational diversity of engine-driven transients.
analysis.result: The transient experienced an ultra-rapid optical rise with $u$-band brightening of $\Delta m_u = 2.45 \pm 0.11\ \mathrm{mag}$ within $\approx 3\ \mathrm{days}$ ($t_{1/2,\mathrm{rise}} = 2.20^{+0.10}_{-0.09}\ \mathrm{days}$, $t_{1/2} < 6\ \mathrm{days}$). analysis.reason: SN 2025wiu presents an extraordinarily slow light-curve evolution and a rare, prominent post-maximum bump in a Type Ib supernova, offering stringent constraints on shock cooling and circumstellar medium interaction mechanisms.
analysis.result: The optical peak exhibits absolute magnitudes $M_{u}=-17.5\pm 0.1$, $M_{g}=-18.11\pm 0.01$, and $M_{r}=-18.24\pm 0.04\,\mathrm{mag}$, with an early excess consistent with shock-cooling emission from a progenitor of $R_{\star} \sim 4\,R_{\odot}$. A post-maximum bump emerges $\sim 23\,\mathrm{d}$ after maximum, peaking at $L_{\mathrm{peak}} \sim 2.4\times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with a duration of $\sim 42\,\mathrm{d}$. Arnett's rule yields $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.47\,M_\odot$ for the main peak, whereas late-time decay indicates $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.13^{+0.05}_{-0.02}\,M_\odot$, and delayed interaction with circumstellar material of mass $M_{\mathrm{CSM}} \sim 0.03\,M_{\odot}$ at $R \sim 5\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{cm}$ (for $\epsilon = 0.5$ and $v_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 8000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) naturally explains the feature.
analysis.reading_entry: VI Bump Properties and Potential Energy Sources
analysis.problem: The light curve of SN 2025wiu exhibits an extraordinary post-maximum bump that deviates markedly from radioactive decay models (${}^{56}\mathrm{Ni}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Co}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$), and the discrepancy between the Arnett-derived peak nickel mass ($0.47\,M_\odot$) and tail-derived nickel mass ($0.13\,M_\odot$) rules out pure radioactive powering.
analysis.method: Multi-band photometry and optical spectroscopy were acquired with WFST, NOT, and SALT. Early shock cooling was modeled using compact progenitor parameters ($R_\star=4\,R_\odot$, $M_{\mathrm{ej}}=2\,M_\odot$, $E=10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$). Light-curve energetics and timescales were modeled using the Arnett analytical relation, the generalized diffusion relation $L_{\mathrm{peak}}=\frac{2}{(\beta t_{\mathrm{peak}})^{2}}\int_{0}^{\beta t_{\mathrm{peak}}}\tau L_{\mathrm{heat}}(\tau)\,d\tau$, gamma-ray deposition $f_{\mathrm{dep}}(t) = 1-\exp[-(T_0/t)^2]$, and diffusion timescale $t_{\mathrm{d}}=\sqrt{3\kappa M_{\mathrm{ej}}/(4\pi v_{\mathrm{ej}}c)}$.
assumptions: The ejecta opacity remains approximately constant across the analytical framework.
A typical magnetar flare timescale is exceptionally short compared to diffusion ($\Delta t_{\mathrm{flare}}\ll t_{\mathrm{d}}$).
limits: Lack of narrow H/He emission lines at $+110\,\mathrm{d}$ limits visible unshocked dense CSM interaction, requiring hidden or asymmetric geometry.

analysis.reason: This paper presents AttNPE, an interpretable neural posterior estimation framework for fast radio burst cosmology that bypasses expensive likelihood evaluations while explicitly capturing source-level redshift contributions to cosmological and host dispersion measure parameters.
analysis.result: AttNPE infers seven cosmological and astrophysical parameters from 120 localized FRBs, obtaining $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.3107^{+0.0254}_{-0.0215}$ and constraining the degenerate composite parameter $\mathcal{A} \equiv H_0\Omega_{\rm b}f_{\rm d}$. The posterior matches MCMC benchmarks with Jensen-Shannon divergence $\mathrm{JSD} < 0.0043$ and $68\%$ credible interval ratio $r_{68} \in [0.993, 1.095]$. While single-source sensitivity $\Delta\mathrm{NLL}_i$ grows with redshift $z$, intermediate-redshift sources ($0.3 \le z < 0.7$, 40 FRBs) dominate the total attention ($46.2\%$) and posterior response for $\Omega_{\rm m}$ ($44.8\%$), $\Omega_{\rm b}$, and $H_0$ due to the scarcity of high-redshift detections ($z \ge 0.7$, 6 FRBs).
analysis.reading_entry: II.1 FRB dispersion model and conditional likelihood
analysis.problem: Joint Bayesian cosmological inference from localized FRBs requires convolving and marginalizing individual sightline dispersion measure components (Galactic halo $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm halo}$, intergalactic medium $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm IGM}$, and host galaxy $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm host}/(1+z)$), resulting in prohibitive likelihood evaluation costs in standard MCMC analyses.
analysis.method: The framework models extragalactic dispersion as $\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm E},i} = \mathrm{DM}_{{\rm halo},i} + \mathrm{DM}_{{\rm IGM},i} + \frac{\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm host},i}}{1+z_i}$ with mean IGM relation $\langle\mathrm{DM}_{\rm IGM}(z)\rangle = \frac{3cH_0\Omega_{\rm b}f_{\rm d}}{8\pi Gm_p}\int_0^z \frac{\chi_e(z')(1+z')}{E(z')}\,\mathrm{d}z'$. It combines a self-attention catalog embedding with a conditional masked autoregressive flow (MAF) to infer $\bm{\theta} = \{\Omega_{\rm m}, \Omega_{\rm b}, H_0, f_{\rm d}, F, \mu_{\rm host}, \sigma_{\rm host}\}$ trained over $10^6$ forward simulations conditioned on the 120 observed FRB redshifts.
assumptions: All simulated catalogs fix the 120 source redshifts to match the observed catalog, with index $i$ corresponding to redshift $z_i$ throughout.
limits: The sample is limited to 120 localized FRBs meeting $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm E} > 80\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ and $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm ISM} \le 0.4\,\mathrm{DM}_{\rm obs}$, with only 6 events at $z \ge 0.7$.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “develop an attention-based neural posterior estimator (AttNPE) for joint inference”
I Introduction: “joint inference of seven cosmological and astrophysical parameters from localized FRB catalogs.”
II.2 FRB sample and mock catalogs: “All simulated catalogs use the same 120 source redshifts as the observed catalog”
III.1 Reliability of the inferred posterior: “We evaluate the calibration of AttNPE on independent simulations using marginal PP curves”
IV Conclusion: “reproduce the reference posterior rapidly while revealing how the estimator uses sources at different redshifts.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates simulation-based neural posterior estimation achieving indistinguishable fidelity to exact MCMC ($\mathrm{JSD} < 10^{-2}$, $r_{68} \approx 1$) while incorporating attention-based diagnostics that quantitatively map parameter sensitivity across the $\langle\mathrm{DM}_{\rm IGM}(z)\rangle$ relation.

The right matrix gives the bin sums of the AttNPE posterior-mean shift $R_{id}$ obtained from held-out simulated catalogs after single-source DM replacement. Each row is normalized over the four bins, and the cell labels give percentages. $H_{0}$ is in units of $\rm km~s^{-1}~Mpc^{-1}$.

(b) Fraction of the total attention obtained by summing source weights within each redshift bin.
figures.label: Fig. 5

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first self-consistent 3D radiative transfer simulations that successfully reproduce the early bolometric and multi-band spectral evolution of AT2017gfo, demonstrating that an ad-hoc separate lanthanide-poor component is unnecessary when realistic 3D ejecta geometry and slower post-merger outflow velocity distributions are taken into account.
analysis.result: Scaling ejecta mass to $M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 0.04\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ and halving velocities (median velocity $v_r \lesssim 0.09c$) matches the bolometric light curve of AT2017gfo within $\sim 30\%$ at $1.5\text{--}5\,\mathrm{d}$ and reproduces early spectra at $1.4$, $2.4$, and $3.4\,\mathrm{d}$. Velocity compression elevates density by a factor of 8 ($V \propto v_r^3$), increasing $\gamma$-ray thermalization efficiency from $\sim 0.3$ to $\sim 0.55$ at $1.4\,\mathrm{d}$ and trapping UVOIR radiation so that late ($6\text{--}12\,\mathrm{d}$) luminosity exceeds instantaneous radioactive deposition by $50\%\text{--}80\%$. The photospheric radius scales as $R_{\mathrm{ph}} = v_{\mathrm{ph}} t$ and effective temperature follows $T_{\mathrm{eff}} \propto L^{1/4} (v_{\mathrm{ph}} t)^{-1/2}$. Distinct transitions are identified: the $\sim 10\,500\,\text{\AA}$ peak is driven by $\mathrm{Sr\;II}\,\lambda\lambda 10037, 10327, 10915$; the $\sim 7300\,\text{\AA}$ peak by $\mathrm{Y\;II}\,\lambda 7882$; and the $\sim 13\,500\,\text{\AA}$ shoulder by $\mathrm{La\;III}\,\lambda\lambda 13894, 14096$ and $\mathrm{Gd\;III}\,\lambda 14333$. In 3D geometry with $\sim 25\%$ mass in low-lanthanide regions ($X_{\mathrm{lan}} < 10^{-3}$), optical flux at $4500\text{--}5500\,\text{\AA}$ is reproduced without an independent lanthanide-free component. In contrast, 2D azimuthally averaged models mix lanthanides into polar sightlines, reducing $1\,\mathrm{d}$ luminosity threefold and producing an excessively red spectrum. Furthermore, standard expansion opacity overestimates uncollided packet transmission $P_0 = e^{-\tau_{\mathrm{bin}}} \approx e^{-1} \approx 0.37$ for optically thick lines ($\tau_l \gg 1$), overestimating early spectral flux by $10\%\text{--}20\%$.
analysis.problem: Previous 3D dynamical ejecta models possessed insufficient mass ($M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 0.005\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) and excessively high velocities relative to empirical inferences for AT2017gfo ($M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 0.03\text{--}0.05\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$), leaving unresolved whether early blue and optical emissions require an independent, distinct lanthanide-poor ejecta component and whether common 2D azimuthal averaging and expansion opacity approximations distort inferred physical properties.
analysis.method: Simulations utilize the 3D time-dependent Monte Carlo radiative transfer code ARTIS with homologous expansion ($r = v_r t$) mapped from a $2 \times 1.35\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ SPH binary neutron star merger snapshot at $t_{\mathrm{snap}} = 0.1\,\mathrm{d}$. Nuclear heating solves the Bateman equations for $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $^{254}\mathrm{Cf}$ fission, tracking non-instantaneous density-dependent charged particle thermalization and $\gamma$-ray transport. Ionization and excitation are treated in LTE via Saha-Boltzmann equations at local electron temperature $T_e$. Calculations employ the AD3 dataset containing $\approx 4.9 \times 10^7$ bound-bound transitions across 323 ions of 83 elements with wavelength-calibrated lanthanide levels. Radiative transfer benchmarks line-by-line (LBL) macroatom treatments against capped line-binned opacities with optical depth $\tau_{\mathrm{bin}} = \sum_i \min(\tau_i, \tau_{\mathrm{l,max}})$ and expansion opacities $\tau_{\mathrm{bin}} = \sum_i (1 - e^{-\tau_i})$.
assumptions: Homologous expansion ($r = v_r t$, $V \propto v_r^3$) from $t_{\mathrm{snap}} = 0.1\,\mathrm{d}$ onward.
limits: Velocity compression is an ad-hoc phenomenological scaling to mimic slower post-merger disk outflows rather than a self-consistent hydrodynamic simulation.

analysis.reason: This paper presents detailed NICER timing and time-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the brightest thermonuclear burst in the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658, providing critical observational constraints on burst-disc interaction and accretion physics in compact objects.
analysis.result: Using simultaneous reflection and persistent emission scaling (Model C), the burst peak exhibits an increased persistent scaling factor $f_{a,1}=59.6\pm 0.6$ and sub-unity reflection fractions $f_{r,1}=0.82\pm 0.15$ and $f_{r,2}=0.55\pm 0.06$. The direct burst bolometric luminosity peaks at $L_{\rm bol} \approx 0.68\,L_{\rm Edd}$, below the Eddington limit despite PRE characteristics. In the burst tail ($>200\,\mathrm{s}$), the absorption column density increases by $\approx 34\%$ ($N_{\mathrm{H}} = (2.42^{+0.13}_{-0.10})\times 10^{21}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$) and the accretion disc temperature increases by $\approx 15\%$ ($kT_{\mathrm{disc}} = 0.78^{+0.04}_{-0.03}\,\mathrm{keV}$), confirming burst-induced disc heating and geometric puffing.
analysis.reading_entry: 6.1.3 Simultaneous Signatures of Reflection & an Evolving Persistent Component (Model C)
analysis.problem: Investigating the physical origin of the soft X-ray excess ($<1.5\,\mathrm{keV}$) during super-bright thermonuclear bursts, the thermodynamic and structural impact of burst irradiation on the accretion disc, and whether persistent accretion emission evolves during the burst.
analysis.method: Performed energy-resolved light curve analysis and time-resolved X-ray spectroscopy ($0.5-10\,\mathrm{keV}$) using NICER. Tested three spectral configurations: variable disc blackbody (Model A, $\mathrm{tbabs} \times (\mathrm{bbodyrad} + \mathrm{diskbb} + \mathrm{nthcomp} + \mathrm{gauss})$), relativistic reflection (Model B, with $\mathrm{rdblur} \times \mathrm{bbrefl}$), and simultaneous reflection plus persistent emission scaling (Model C, combining reflection with the $f_a$-method where $F_{\rm pers} = f_a F_{\rm pers,0}$), extended into the burst tail ($>200\,\mathrm{s}$) and pre-burst phase.
assumptions: Iron abundance $A_{\rm Fe}$ can be tied across burst peak spectra.

analysis.reason: The paper provides a rapid multi-messenger Bayesian inference framework combining binary neutron star gravitational waves, NICER X-ray timing, and radio pulsar observations to constrain the dense matter equation of state, yielding precise joint limits on neutron star structural parameters.
analysis.result: Joint inference from gravitational-wave, X-ray, and radio pulsar datasets constrains the typical neutron star radius to $R_{1.4}=11.93^{+1.02}_{-0.83}\,\mathrm{km}$ and the maximum non-rotating neutron star mass to $M_{\rm max}=2.31^{+0.23}_{-0.23}\,M_{\odot}$ at $90\%$ credible level, disfavoring overly soft or stiff equations of state across nuclear densities.
analysis.problem: Constraining the cold ultra-dense matter equation of state across nuclear saturation and super-saturation regimes, reconciling observational constraints from independent probes that sample distinct density and pressure domains.
analysis.method: The authors apply a rapid hierarchical Bayesian inference scheme (GWXtreme) that evaluates joint evidence across BNS gravitational waves, NICER X-ray pulse profile modeling, and radio pulsar mass measurements using kernel density estimation likelihood approximations and a four-parameter spectral representation $\ln\Gamma(p,\vec{\gamma})=\sum_{k=0}^{3}\gamma_k(\ln(p/p_o))^k$ subject to causal and stability bounds.

analysis.reason: This paper develops a Bayesian framework combining FRB dispersion measures and mock galaxy surveys in IllustrisTNG to deconstruct the cosmic baryon distribution across cosmic web environments, directly relevant to FRB propagation and baryon census studies.
analysis.result: The reconstruction accurately recovers the cosmic ionized baryon density as $\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}f_{\mathrm{ion}} = 0.0455^{+0.0028}_{-0.0026}$ (consistent with the IllustrisTNG true value of $0.0462$ at the $0.2\sigma$ level), corresponding to $\Omega_{\mathrm{b}} = 0.0479^{+0.0029}_{-0.0027}$ for $f_{\mathrm{ion}} = 0.95$. Approximately $75\%$ of free electrons reside in diffuse low-density environments ($\rho_{\mathrm{m}}/\rho_{\mathrm{crit}} \le 2.94$). Inferred gas mass fractions across structures are $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{void}} = 0.186 \pm 0.012$, $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{filament}} = 0.179 \pm 0.015$, and $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{halo}} = 0.046 \pm 0.014$ (against true values $0.167$, $0.173$, and $0.067$), recovering $98.60\%$ of global ionized baryons ($\langle r_{\mathrm{FRB}} \rangle_M = 0.986\,r_{\mathrm{theo}}$).
analysis.problem: Cosmological dispersion measure $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{LSS}}(\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}, z) = \frac{3cH_0\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}}{8\pi G m_{\mathrm{p}}} f_{\mathrm{ion}} f_{\mathrm{e}} \int_0^z \frac{1+z'}{E(z')} [1+\delta_{\mathrm{e}}(\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}, z')]\,\mathrm{d}z'$ is an integrated line-of-sight quantity that cannot directly resolve the local spatial density contrast $\delta_{\mathrm{e}}$ and electron distribution across distinct cosmic web environments (voids, filaments, and halos).
analysis.method: Using IllustrisTNG TNG300-1 simulations ($z \in [0, 1.5]$), large-scale structure is partitioned into $M=8$ logarithmic matter density bins. A discrete linear forward system $\mathbf{d} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{r} + \mathbf{n}$ relates line-of-sight DM to electron-to-matter density ratios $r_i = n_{\mathrm{e}, i}/\rho_i$, with theoretical expectation $r_{\mathrm{theo}} = \frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}}{\Omega_{\mathrm{m}}\mu_{\mathrm{e}}m_{\mathrm{p}}} f_{\mathrm{ion}} \approx (7.84 \pm 0.18) \times 10^{22}\,\mathrm{g}^{-1}$. A 4-parameter profile $\mathbf{r}(\theta)$ parameterized by $\theta = \{\mathcal{S}, \log\rho_{\mathrm{tran}}, w_{\rho}, \alpha_{\rho}\}$ is sampled via MCMC (`emcee`) across $N=470$ quasi-independent lines of sight ($|R_{ij}| < 0.3$). Visible matter density from a simulated Euclid-like galaxy survey $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{gal}} = \bar{\rho}_{\mathrm{m}}[1 + \delta_{\mathrm{gal}}/b]$ is combined to reconstruct $\hat{n}_{\mathrm{e}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{FRB}} \cdot \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{gal}}$.
assumptions: AGN and supernova feedback drive hot gas outward from central halos into outskirts, suppressing the electron-to-matter density ratio $r(\theta)$ in high-density regions relative to $r_{\mathrm{theo}}$.
limits: Severe spectroscopic incompleteness (e.g. 80% galaxy subsampling) reduces density reconstruction accuracy by 27%–31% in low-density bins and 46%–53% in high-density bins, and redshift-space distortions (RSD) introduce interpolation biases along the line of sight.

analysis.reason: This study models the Galactic population of dormant neutron star binaries and forecasts Gaia DR4/DR5 astrometric yields, providing quantitative constraints on core-collapse supernova engines, natal kicks, and dense matter equations of state.
analysis.result: Under the realistic selection function gaiamock, Gaia is predicted to detect $\sim 100\text{--}110$ and $\sim 300\text{--}380$ dormant neutron star--luminous companion (NS--LC) binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively. In the intrinsic population, $\sim 94\%$ of surviving detached systems survive through common envelope (CE) evolution ($P_{\rm orb} \le 10\,\mathrm{yr}$). The observed NS mass distribution peaks sharply at $1.2\text{--}1.3\,M_\odot$ driven by low-kick ($\sigma = 20\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) electron-capture supernovae (ECSN), while delayed core-collapse supernova (CCSN) fallback produces massive NSs exceeding $M_{\rm NS} > 2.5\,M_\odot$ in $\sim 1\%$ of systems. Pulsar spin-down and magnetic field decay follow $\dot{P}_{\rm spin} = K \frac{B^2}{P_{\rm spin}}$ ($K = 9.87 \times 10^{-48}\,\mathrm{yr\,G^{-2}}$), death line $B/P_{\rm spin}^2 = 0.17 \times 10^{12}\,\mathrm{G\,s^{-2}}$, and accretion-induced burial $B = \frac{B_0}{1 + \Delta M / (10^{-6}\,M_\odot)} \exp\left(-\frac{T - t_{\rm acc}}{\tau}\right)$ with $\tau = 3\,\mathrm{Gyr}$.
analysis.problem: Quantifying the Galactic population of dormant neutron stars in detached binaries with luminous companions (NS--LC) detectable via astrometric orbital wobbles in Gaia DR4 and DR5, and testing whether their yields and orbital parameters can break degeneracies between core-collapse supernova explosion models (rapid vs. delayed), natal kicks ($\sigma = 265\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ vs. $20\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$), and common envelope evolution.
analysis.method: Binary population synthesis using COSMIC initialized with a Kroupa IMF ($3 < m_{\rm pri}/M_\odot < 60$), flat mass ratios ($q = m_{\rm sec}/m_{\rm pri}$), thermal eccentricities, and log-flat semi-major axes up to $10^5\,R_\odot$. Spatial distribution and star formation histories are drawn from the FIRE-2 m12i Milky Way simulation ($10^{-4} \le Z \le 0.03$). Supernova prescriptions incorporate rapid and delayed core-collapse models (maximum $M_{\rm NS} = 3\,M_\odot$), ECSN ($M_{\rm ZAMS} \sim 8\text{--}10\,M_\odot$, $M_{\rm Ch} \approx 1.38\,M_\odot$), and accretion-induced collapse (AIC), followed by synthetic observation through CCB22 and gaiamock astrometric selection functions.
assumptions: The Milky Way binary population follows star formation and metallicity distributions from the FIRE-2 m12i simulation evaluated across 100 Galactic realizations.
limits: The isolated binary evolution models produce no detached millisecond pulsars (MSPs) with main-sequence companions, in contrast to 29 known field radio MSPs in tight orbits from the ATNF pulsar catalog.

analysis.reason: The paper develops a unified Poynting-flux-dominated jet model connecting fast X-ray transients (FXTs) to gamma-ray bursts via premature magnetic dissipation when the jet satisfies the causal condition $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma < 1$.
analysis.result: Premature kink instability dissipates Poynting flux at stellar breakout radius $R_* \sim 10^{11}\,\mathrm{cm}$ with Lorentz factor $\Gamma \sim 20$, yielding rapid thermalization where mean comoving photon energy $\langle E' \rangle \sim 2.7 k_{\rm B} [L_{\rm iso}/(4\pi R_*^2 \Gamma^2 a c)]^{1/4} \sim 0.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ escapes as soft X-rays with thermalization timescale $\tau_{\rm th} \sim N_{\rm th} R_* / (\ell' c)$, minimum variability timescale $\Delta t_{\rm var} \simeq (1+z) R_{\rm ph} \theta_{\rm J}^2 / (2c) \sim 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{s}$, and no jet breaks because $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma < 1$ holds throughout.
analysis.problem: Explaining the physical nature of fast X-ray transients (FXTs) associated with type Ic-BL supernovae that exhibit soft thermal X-ray spectra, low peak energies, long deceleration times, and an absence of geometric jet breaks.
analysis.method: Modeling Blandford–Znajek driven Poynting-flux-dominated jets with initial magnetization $\sigma_0 \gg 1$ accelerating via ideal MHD magnetic pressure gradient as $\Gamma(R) = \sigma_0^{3/2}(R/R_{\rm sat})^{1/3}$, where global kink instability triggers premature dissipation at $R_*$ if $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R_*) < 1$.
assumptions: The relativistic jet is Poynting-flux dominated with initial magnetization $\sigma_0 \equiv \dot{E}_{\rm Poynting}/\dot{E}_{\rm kinetic} \gg 1$ accelerating as $\Gamma(R) \propto R^{1/3}$ before saturation.
limits: Global kink instability requires the entire jet cross-section to remain causally connected under $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R) < 1$.
citation_leads: II The model: “if the jet opening angle $\theta_{\rm J}$ satisfies $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R)<1”
III Confronting observations: “$\theta_{J}\Gamma<1$ holds at all times, so no jet break is expected regardless of the opening angle.”
References: “A fast X-ray transient from a weak relativistic jet associated with a type Ic-BL supernova.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that a critical magnetization threshold $\sigma_0 \approx 45$ divides premature-dissipated FXTs ($\sigma_0 \lesssim 45$, $\Gamma \lesssim 50$) from standard GRBs ($\sigma_0 > 45$, $\Gamma > 100$), naturally reproducing FXT thermal spectra and lack of jet breaks within relativistic jet physics.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic of the jet evolution scenario. A Poynting-flux-dominated jet is launched from the central engine and propagates through the progenitor envelope. Kink instability may develops in the magnetically dominated flow, triggering premature magnetic dissipation at low Lorentz factor, producing the fast X-ray transient (FXT). In the sketch, we also plot the case when the premature dissipation is absence, the jet continues accelerating to ultra-relativistic Lorentz factor and produces a classical gamma-ray burst (GRB) via dissipation at larger radii.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: Schematic of the unified jet evolution scenario: a Poynting-flux-dominated jet launched from the central engine either suffers kink instability triggering premature magnetic dissipation at low Lorentz factor ($\\Gamma \\lesssim 50$) inside the envelope to produce a fast X-ray transient (FXT), or avoids premature dissipation to accelerate to ultra-relativistic velocities ($\\Gamma > 100$) and dissipate at larger radii ($\\sim 10^{15}\\text{ cm}$) as a classical gamma-ray burst (GRB).

analysis.reason: This paper presents an unprecedented, continuously monitored common envelope evolution event and stellar merger in M31 (AT 2025abao), directly probing circumstellar material (CSM) interaction and plateau emission mechanisms relevant to shock interaction and plateau studies in transients.
analysis.result: The progenitor is identified as an early AGB star ($M_1 \approx 7\,M_\odot$, $R_{\rm eff} \approx 350\,R_\odot$, $L \approx 1.8 \times 10^4\,L_\odot$, $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-5}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr^{-1}}$) with a low-mass companion ($M_2 \approx 0.7\,M_\odot$, mass ratio $q=0.10_{-0.08}^{+0.10}$). The 7-year precursor brightening ($L_{\rm drag} \approx 3 \times 10^{38}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$) was driven by frictional drag in the primary's convective envelope, transitioning to a dynamic plunge and luminous red nova eruption with ejecta kinetic energy $KE_{\rm ej} \sim 10^{48}\,{\rm erg}$ and unbound mass $\sim 0.2\text{--}0.4\,M_\odot$, whose optical plateau is powered by momentum-conserving shock interaction with equatorial CSM having $\rho(r) \propto r^{-2}$.
analysis.problem: How orbital energy is partitioned and dissipated during common envelope evolution (CEE), and whether standard $\alpha$-formalisms adequately describe envelope unbinding versus ejecta kinetic acceleration and shock interactions with pre-existing CSM.
analysis.method: Multi-epoch photometric monitoring (ZTF, WINTER, SPHEREx, Cerberus 1-second cadence) and spectroscopic follow-up (Gemini/GMOS, FIES, NIRES, JWST/MIRI MRS), combined with PHOENIX stellar atmosphere and DUSTY radiative transfer SED fitting via emcee MCMC, alongside momentum-conserving shock deceleration modeling of the ejecta-CSM interaction.

figures.caption: Figure 10: A graphical representation of the different phases of AT 2025abao. a) The quiescent binary system comprising a $\approx 7$ M ⊙ AGB and a $\approx 0.7$ M ⊙ star, surrounded by an extended dust shell from mass loss from the binary following Roche Lobe overflow of the primary. b) The precursor brightening phase that began in 2018, marking the onset of CEE, powered by frictional drag on the inspiraling companion lasting for $\approx 7$ years. The mass outflow rate during this phase is $\sim 10^{-2}$ M ⊙ yr -1, producing $\sim 0.1$ M ⊙ of CBM in an equatorial disk around the binary (dark brown), c) The ballistic eruption in late 2025 from the merger of the inspiraling companion with the primary core, resulting in the ejection of $\approx 0.1-0.2$ M ⊙ of the primary envelope, and sublimation of a large fraction of dust around the binary. d) The eventual lightcurve powered by shock-interactions between freely expanding merger ejecta (indicated by yellow arrows) and equatorially focused CBM. The surviving pre-existing dust is traced by our JWST observations. The black arrows between the panels indicate the progression of time.
figures.label: Fig. 10
figures.physical_core: A four-stage schematic illustrating the full physical lifecycle of Common Envelope Evolution (CEE) in AT 2025abao: (a) the quiescent binary ($\approx 7\,M_\odot$ AGB primary and $\approx 0.7\,M_\odot$ companion) with pre-existing dust from Roche Lobe overflow; (b) a $\approx 7$-year precursor brightening powered by frictional drag dissipation during companion inspiral through the convective envelope ($\\dot{M} \sim 10^{-2}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$); (c) ballistic envelope ejection ($\\approx 0.1\text{--}0.2\,M_\odot$) triggered by the core merger; and (d) subsequent shock interaction between merger ejecta and equatorial circumstellar matter.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Understanding CEE. Top Left: Peak precursor luminosity versus primary escape speed for AT 2025abao, V1309Sco [ 17 ], and M31-LRN-2015 [ 22 ], colored by precursor duration in orbital periods at the primary’s surface. Lines show the kinetic luminosity of outflows at various mass-loss rates (dashed gray, Equation 5 ) and drag luminosity from an inspiraling companion (red, Equation 7 ) for the mass ratios in the legend. Top right: Theoretical estimates of dust mass around the quiescent progenitor (black line: analytical, squares: MESA simulations) versus that ejected during the precursor (Section 1.4.3 ), colored by binary mass ratio. The shaded region spans the progenitor dust range by varying the analytical-model parameters (Section 1.4.2 ). The red star shows measured values with 1 $\sigma$ uncertainties. Bottom left: Envelope binding energy versus radius (black) from the MESA model of the 7 M ⊙, 340 R ⊙ AGB primary star, inferred orbital energy dissipated by the companion (red), observed ejecta kinetic energy (blue), and observed radiated energy during the precursor (green). Solid lines are median values, shaded regions mark 1 $\sigma$ uncertainties. Bottom Right: CE efficiency $\alpha$ versus binary mass ratio. The inferred mass ratio and its 1 $\sigma$ uncertainty is marked with the purple solid line and shaded region. Black shaded regions are ruled out by a core-merger in this system and its observed ejected mass. Black points show $\alpha$ measurements from post-CE binary systems [ 50 ] (Section 1.4.6 ).
figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: Comprehensive theoretical and empirical diagnostic of CEE energetics and parameters: compares inspiral drag luminosity and outflow kinetic luminosity against precursor properties; contrasts the MESA primary envelope binding energy $E_{\mathrm{bind}}(r)$ with dissipated orbital energy $\Delta E_{\mathrm{orb}}$, ejecta kinetic energy $E_{\mathrm{kin}}$, and radiated energy $E_{\mathrm{rad}}$; and establishes empirical constraints on the common envelope efficiency parameter $0.01 \lesssim \alpha \lesssim 0.4$ as a function of binary mass ratio $q$.

analysis.reason: The paper develops a parameter-free, high-order smoothness indicator for AMR in Newtonian, SRMHD, and GRMHD simulations, demonstrating robust tracking of relativistic blast waves and black hole accretion flows with significant speedups.
analysis.result: The indicator accurately captures discontinuities and shear layers across tests: in Kelvin–Helmholtz instability tests with $\Gamma=5/3$ and effective resolution $2048^{2}$, it speeds up computation by $1.45\times$; in SRMHD magnetic rotor tests, it achieves a $3.4\times$ reduction in MeshBlock-cycles and $2.8\times$ wall-clock speedup; in GRMHD MAD simulations around Kerr black holes ($a/M_{\rm BH}=0.9, \phi_{\rm BH} = \Phi_{\rm BH}/\sqrt{\dot{M}} \gtrsim 15$), it successfully resolves jet launching, though computational savings diminish when the region $r \le 100r_g$ becomes fully turbulent.
analysis.problem: High computational cost and lack of problem-independent, robust error indicators for adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) in multi-dimensional Newtonian, SRMHD, and GRMHD simulations.
analysis.method: Adapted from spectral modal falloff indicators, the scheme calculates the 4th-order undivided finite difference $\Delta^{(4)}u = u_{i+2}-4u_{i+1}+6u_{i}-4u_{i-1}+u_{i-2}$ over a symmetric 5-point stencil to obtain the oscillation measure $e_i = |\Delta^{(4)}u/u_i|$, applying fixed thresholds $4^{-2}=0.0625$ for refinement and $4^{-3}=0.015625$ for coarsening across conserved variables $(D, M^j, E, B^j)$ in AthenaK.
assumptions: Monitored physical fields are sufficiently smooth away from true discontinuities such that high-order polynomial modal coefficients decay rapidly.
limits: AMR computational savings diminish once turbulence fills the entire domain of interest (such as fully developed post-eruption MAD states at $r \le 100r_g$), and initial discontinuities require pre-refinement to prevent staircasing artifacts.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first binary population synthesis coupled with time-dependent synchrotron nebular models for hyper-Eddington mass-transfer systems, directly constraining persistent radio source (PRS) counterparts to repeating FRBs, relativistic jet inflation, and radio transient surveys.
analysis.result: The local volumetric birth rate of hyper-Eddington mass-transfer binaries is $\mathcal{R} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ spanning $\dot{m} \sim 10^{2\text{--}7}$ and accretion timescales $t_{\rm acc} \sim 10^{0\text{--}6}\,\mathrm{yr}$. The systems launch mildly relativistic jets ($v_{\rm j} \sim 0.1\text{--}0.3c$) and disk winds ($v_{\rm w} \sim 0.03c$) inflating long-lived synchrotron hypernebulae with peak radio luminosities $L_{\nu,\rm peak} \sim 10^{28}\text{--}10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$ at $\sim 1\text{--}3\,\mathrm{GHz}$, overlapping with FRB-associated PRSs and yielding $\sim 10^{2\text{--}5}$ detectable steady sources in VLASS.
analysis.problem: Distinguishing unresolved synchrotron hypernebulae driven by rare, energetic hyper-Eddington binary mass transfer from other populations of unresolved synchrotron sources (such as AGNs, SNRs, and GRB afterglows) in modern wide-field radio surveys.
analysis.method: Coupled COMPAS binary population synthesis (v02.35.03) with a semi-analytic synchrotron hypernebula model. For stable RLOF, the mass-transfer rate is set by donor envelope thermal timescale $\dot{M} = \dot{M}_{\rm th} = M_{\rm d,env}/\tau_{\rm KH} = R_{\rm d}L_{\rm d}/(G M_{\rm d})$ with duration $t_{\rm acc} = \tau_{\rm KH}$, whereas unstable common-envelope evolution incorporates pre-dynamical accretion $\dot{M} = f_{\rm acc}\Delta M_{\rm CE}/(100 P_{\rm orb})$. Jet kinetic luminosity scales as $L_{\rm j} = \eta L_{\rm w} \simeq \frac{1}{2}\eta \dot{M} v_{\rm w}^2$ with efficiency $\eta \sim 0.1$, injecting relativistic electrons at the termination shock.
assumptions: The donor star transfers its envelope onto a compact object (NS or BH) at hyper-Eddington rates $\dot{M} \gtrsim \dot{M}_{\rm Edd} \equiv L_{\rm Edd}/(0.1c^2)$.
limits: VLBI observations with milliarcsecond-scale resolution are insensitive to diffuse parsec-scale hypernebula structures.

analysis.reason: This paper provides valuable observational and theoretical constraints on neutron star crustal heating mechanisms by utilizing carbon burning instability to break the degeneracy between shallow and deep heating in KS 1731-260, offering key insights for compact object high-energy thermal evolution.
analysis.result: Enforcing the local carbon ignition instability criterion $(\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm C}}{\partial T})_P \ge (\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm cool}}{\partial T})_P$ breaks the degeneracy of quiescent cooling fits and strongly favors shallow heating overlapping the carbon fuel layer at column depth $y_* = 0.630\times 10^{12}\text{ g cm}^{-2}$. Deeper heating ($\log_{10}P = 27\text{--}28\text{ dyn cm}^{-2}$) requires nearly twice the heating strength ($q_a = 4.00\text{ MeV nucleon}^{-1}$ vs. $2.19\text{ MeV nucleon}^{-1}$ for shallow heating under CF88 rates), causing severe quiescent spectral residuals ($\Delta W \simeq 352$ vs. $\Delta W \simeq 39$) and overpredicting $2\text{--}3\text{ keV}$ counts by a factor of $\sim 5$. For the superburst decay at $d = 4.5\text{ kpc}$, depth-dependent energy deposition $e_{\rm b}(y) \propto (y/y_{\rm h})^{1/4}$ with $y_{\rm h} = 6.62\times 10^{11}\text{ g cm}^{-2}$ and total burst energy $\mathcal{E}_{\rm b} = 2.19\times 10^{42}\text{ erg}$ (residual sum 10.2) reproduces early cooling significantly better than uniform deposition (residual sum 26.6).
analysis.reading_entry: III.1 The Carbon Instability Condition Favors Shallower Heating
analysis.problem: Quiescent cooling models of accreting neutron star crusts suffer from an intrinsic degeneracy where shallow heating overlapping the fuel layer and deep heating beneath it produce nearly identical surface cooling curves by adjusting heating strength $q_a$ and core temperature $T_{\rm c}$, leaving the true physical depth and origin of shallow accretion heating unconstrained.
analysis.method: Thermal evolution is simulated with the dStar code for a neutron star ($M = 1.4\,M_\odot$, $R = 10\text{ km}$, $d = 4.5\text{ kpc}$) under RXTE/ASM reconstructed accretion rate history $\dot{M}(t)$. The model applies local carbon instability criteria $(\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm C}}{\partial T})_P \ge (\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm cool}}{\partial T})_P$ with local heating rate $\epsilon_a = \frac{\dot{M}Q_a}{M_a m_u}$, conduction cooling $\epsilon_{\rm cool} = 0.17\frac{K\rho T}{y^2}$, thermal conductivity $K = \frac{\pi^2 c^2 k_{\rm B}^2 T n_e}{3\mu_e \nu_{ei}}$, advective carbon burial/consumption $\frac{dy}{dt}$, and burst energy deposition $e_{\rm b}(y) \propto (y/y_{\rm h})^\beta$ (with $\beta = 0$ or $1/4$), followed by joint spectral fitting across 10 Chandra quiescent epochs ($0.5\text{--}7\text{ keV}$) via Nelder–Mead optimization.
assumptions: The carbon mass fraction in the ignition layer is assumed to be $X_{\rm C} = 0.20$ yielding a nuclear energy release of $\approx 2\times 10^{17}\text{ erg g}^{-1}$.
limits: Conductive cooling models predict superburst decay light curves that remain broader than observed (early flux is underpredicted and late tail is overpredicted by a factor of $\sim 3$ even when accounting for $^{23}{\rm Na}$–$^{23}{\rm Ne}$ Urca shell neutrino losses).

analysis.reason: This paper uses ASKAP POSSUM broadband polarization observations to probe statistical depolarization and Faraday dispersion across the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). It provides valuable empirical constraints on the turbulent magneto-ionic medium and thermal electron density scaling in dwarf irregular galaxies, relevant to intervening sightlines and propagation effects of extragalactic transients.
analysis.result: The fraction of polarized sources is significantly suppressed on-SMC ($f_{\mathrm{pol,on}} = 0.227 \pm 0.021$) compared to off-SMC ($f_{\mathrm{pol,off}} = 0.360 \pm 0.015$), accompanied by an enhanced Faraday depth dispersion $\Sigma_{\phi_{\mathrm{peak}}} = 74 \pm 9\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}}$. Modeling external Faraday dispersion with Burn's law gives $\sigma_\phi = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ with $k = 0.32$, implying a tangled random magnetic field strength $B_r = (1.0 \pm 0.2)\,(l_0/0.5\ \mathrm{pc})^{-1/2}\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ ($B_r \approx 0.3\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ at the beam scale $\sim 6\ \mathrm{pc}$).
analysis.problem: Determining whether depolarization of background radio sources in the SMC is driven by small-scale thermal electron density fluctuations or turbulent random magnetic fields, and assessing whether small-scale Faraday dispersion matches extrapolations of the large-scale RM power spectrum.
analysis.method: Subtracted SMC diffuse emission, performed RM synthesis and Stokes $QU$-fitting on POSSUM Pilot II data ($800-1088\ \mathrm{MHz}$), and modeled external Faraday dispersion $\sigma_\phi = 0.812\,n_e\,B_\parallel\,\sqrt{l_0\,L} = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ combined with $\mathrm{H}\alpha$-derived emission measure $\left(\frac{\mathrm{EM}}{\mathrm{cm^{-6}\ pc}}\right) \approx 2.75 \left(\frac{I_{\mathrm{H}\alpha,\mathrm{corr}}}{\mathrm{R}}\right) \left(\frac{T_e}{10^4\ \mathrm{K}}\right)^{0.942}$.
assumptions: Thermal electron density $n_e$ is assumed to be approximately constant across small scales, attributing Faraday dispersion primarily to random magnetic field fluctuations.
limits: Faraday complexity and multi-component structures are predominantly intrinsic to background sources or foreground Milky Way emission rather than SMC magneto-ionic turbulence.

analysis.reason: The paper uses an unseen-species statistical framework on CHIME/FRB repeaters to demonstrate that repeating FRB sources cease activity within a few years rather than emitting steadily, placing strict demographic constraints on young magnetar engines.
analysis.result: Steady Poisson activity is decisively ruled out ($p < 10^{-4}$, with no mock catalog out of 10,000 yielding $S \le 0.530$). The gap ratio $R(\Delta) = n^{\rm obs}/n^{\rm pred} \approx 1$ at $\Delta \lesssim 60\,\mathrm{d}$ decreases by half within one year. Fitting extinction models yields a characteristic lifetime $\tau = 2.9^{+1.1}_{-0.9}\,\mathrm{yr}$ (single lifetime), an active duration $T_{\rm on} = 800^{+400}_{-400}\,\mathrm{days}$ with duty cycle $d = 0.3^{+0.05}_{-0.2}$ (on/off model), or short-lifetime $\tau_s = 500^{+300}_{-200}\,\mathrm{days}$ with long-lived fraction $\eta = 0.3^{+0.2}_{-0.1}$ (mixture model). The implied birth rate satisfies $\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm birth}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm mag}} \sim 0.1 \left(\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm FRB}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm CCSN}}\right) \left(\frac{0.1}{f_{\rm b}}\right) \left(\frac{0.4}{f_{\rm mag}}\right) \left(\frac{100\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}}{\bar{r}}\right)$, indicating only $\sim 10\%$ of newborn magnetars need to be active repeaters.

analysis.problem: Whether repeating FRBs maintain steady Poisson activity over multi-year baselines, and what their true active lifetime is across the source population without being biased by rare hyperactive sources.
analysis.method: Employs Robbins' formula for unseen species estimation, where the burst yield in window $B$ ($T_B$) is predicted from detections $N_{k+1}$ in window $A$ ($T_A$) via $n_k^{\rm pred} = (k+1) N_{k+1} (T_B/T_A)$ independent of rate distribution $f(r)$. Evaluates the gap statistic $R(\Delta) = n^{\rm obs}/n^{\rm pred}$ using sliding windows ($W = 180\,\mathrm{d}$, step $30\,\mathrm{d}$, $k \le 3$), and derives the exposure ratio $t = T_B/T_A$ self-consistently from new source counts via the Good–Toulmin estimator $N_{\rm new} = \sum_{k\ge 1} (-1)^{k+1} t^k N_k$.

analysis.reason: SN 2025wiu presents an extraordinarily slow light-curve evolution and a rare, prominent post-maximum bump in a Type Ib supernova, offering stringent constraints on shock cooling and circumstellar medium interaction mechanisms.
analysis.result: The optical peak exhibits absolute magnitudes $M_{u}=-17.5\pm 0.1$, $M_{g}=-18.11\pm 0.01$, and $M_{r}=-18.24\pm 0.04\,\mathrm{mag}$, with an early excess consistent with shock-cooling emission from a progenitor of $R_{\star} \sim 4\,R_{\odot}$. A post-maximum bump emerges $\sim 23\,\mathrm{d}$ after maximum, peaking at $L_{\mathrm{peak}} \sim 2.4\times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with a duration of $\sim 42\,\mathrm{d}$. Arnett's rule yields $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.47\,M_\odot$ for the main peak, whereas late-time decay indicates $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.13^{+0.05}_{-0.02}\,M_\odot$, and delayed interaction with circumstellar material of mass $M_{\mathrm{CSM}} \sim 0.03\,M_{\odot}$ at $R \sim 5\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{cm}$ (for $\epsilon = 0.5$ and $v_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 8000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) naturally explains the feature.
analysis.reading_entry: VI Bump Properties and Potential Energy Sources
analysis.problem: The light curve of SN 2025wiu exhibits an extraordinary post-maximum bump that deviates markedly from radioactive decay models (${}^{56}\mathrm{Ni}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Co}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$), and the discrepancy between the Arnett-derived peak nickel mass ($0.47\,M_\odot$) and tail-derived nickel mass ($0.13\,M_\odot$) rules out pure radioactive powering.
analysis.method: Multi-band photometry and optical spectroscopy were acquired with WFST, NOT, and SALT. Early shock cooling was modeled using compact progenitor parameters ($R_\star=4\,R_\odot$, $M_{\mathrm{ej}}=2\,M_\odot$, $E=10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$). Light-curve energetics and timescales were modeled using the Arnett analytical relation, the generalized diffusion relation $L_{\mathrm{peak}}=\frac{2}{(\beta t_{\mathrm{peak}})^{2}}\int_{0}^{\beta t_{\mathrm{peak}}}\tau L_{\mathrm{heat}}(\tau)\,d\tau$, gamma-ray deposition $f_{\mathrm{dep}}(t) = 1-\exp[-(T_0/t)^2]$, and diffusion timescale $t_{\mathrm{d}}=\sqrt{3\kappa M_{\mathrm{ej}}/(4\pi v_{\mathrm{ej}}c)}$.
assumptions: The ejecta opacity remains approximately constant across the analytical framework.
A typical magnetar flare timescale is exceptionally short compared to diffusion ($\Delta t_{\mathrm{flare}}\ll t_{\mathrm{d}}$).
limits: Lack of narrow H/He emission lines at $+110\,\mathrm{d}$ limits visible unshocked dense CSM interaction, requiring hidden or asymmetric geometry.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “Its light curve exhibits a prominent post-maximum bump that deviates significantly from pure radioactive decay models, strongly suggesting the presence of an additional powering mechanism.”

analysis.reason: This paper presents AttNPE, an interpretable neural posterior estimation framework for fast radio burst cosmology that bypasses expensive likelihood evaluations while explicitly capturing source-level redshift contributions to cosmological and host dispersion measure parameters.
analysis.result: AttNPE infers seven cosmological and astrophysical parameters from 120 localized FRBs, obtaining $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.3107^{+0.0254}_{-0.0215}$ and constraining the degenerate composite parameter $\mathcal{A} \equiv H_0\Omega_{\rm b}f_{\rm d}$. The posterior matches MCMC benchmarks with Jensen-Shannon divergence $\mathrm{JSD} < 0.0043$ and $68\%$ credible interval ratio $r_{68} \in [0.993, 1.095]$. While single-source sensitivity $\Delta\mathrm{NLL}_i$ grows with redshift $z$, intermediate-redshift sources ($0.3 \le z < 0.7$, 40 FRBs) dominate the total attention ($46.2\%$) and posterior response for $\Omega_{\rm m}$ ($44.8\%$), $\Omega_{\rm b}$, and $H_0$ due to the scarcity of high-redshift detections ($z \ge 0.7$, 6 FRBs).
analysis.reading_entry: II.1 FRB dispersion model and conditional likelihood
analysis.problem: Joint Bayesian cosmological inference from localized FRBs requires convolving and marginalizing individual sightline dispersion measure components (Galactic halo $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm halo}$, intergalactic medium $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm IGM}$, and host galaxy $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm host}/(1+z)$), resulting in prohibitive likelihood evaluation costs in standard MCMC analyses.
analysis.method: The framework models extragalactic dispersion as $\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm E},i} = \mathrm{DM}_{{\rm halo},i} + \mathrm{DM}_{{\rm IGM},i} + \frac{\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm host},i}}{1+z_i}$ with mean IGM relation $\langle\mathrm{DM}_{\rm IGM}(z)\rangle = \frac{3cH_0\Omega_{\rm b}f_{\rm d}}{8\pi Gm_p}\int_0^z \frac{\chi_e(z')(1+z')}{E(z')}\,\mathrm{d}z'$. It combines a self-attention catalog embedding with a conditional masked autoregressive flow (MAF) to infer $\bm{\theta} = \{\Omega_{\rm m}, \Omega_{\rm b}, H_0, f_{\rm d}, F, \mu_{\rm host}, \sigma_{\rm host}\}$ trained over $10^6$ forward simulations conditioned on the 120 observed FRB redshifts.
assumptions: All simulated catalogs fix the 120 source redshifts to match the observed catalog, with index $i$ corresponding to redshift $z_i$ throughout.
limits: The sample is limited to 120 localized FRBs meeting $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm E} > 80\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ and $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm ISM} \le 0.4\,\mathrm{DM}_{\rm obs}$, with only 6 events at $z \ge 0.7$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first self-consistent 3D radiative transfer simulations that successfully reproduce the early bolometric and multi-band spectral evolution of AT2017gfo, demonstrating that an ad-hoc separate lanthanide-poor component is unnecessary when realistic 3D ejecta geometry and slower post-merger outflow velocity distributions are taken into account.
analysis.result: Scaling ejecta mass to $M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 0.04\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ and halving velocities (median velocity $v_r \lesssim 0.09c$) matches the bolometric light curve of AT2017gfo within $\sim 30\%$ at $1.5\text{--}5\,\mathrm{d}$ and reproduces early spectra at $1.4$, $2.4$, and $3.4\,\mathrm{d}$. Velocity compression elevates density by a factor of 8 ($V \propto v_r^3$), increasing $\gamma$-ray thermalization efficiency from $\sim 0.3$ to $\sim 0.55$ at $1.4\,\mathrm{d}$ and trapping UVOIR radiation so that late ($6\text{--}12\,\mathrm{d}$) luminosity exceeds instantaneous radioactive deposition by $50\%\text{--}80\%$. The photospheric radius scales as $R_{\mathrm{ph}} = v_{\mathrm{ph}} t$ and effective temperature follows $T_{\mathrm{eff}} \propto L^{1/4} (v_{\mathrm{ph}} t)^{-1/2}$. Distinct transitions are identified: the $\sim 10\,500\,\text{\AA}$ peak is driven by $\mathrm{Sr\;II}\,\lambda\lambda 10037, 10327, 10915$; the $\sim 7300\,\text{\AA}$ peak by $\mathrm{Y\;II}\,\lambda 7882$; and the $\sim 13\,500\,\text{\AA}$ shoulder by $\mathrm{La\;III}\,\lambda\lambda 13894, 14096$ and $\mathrm{Gd\;III}\,\lambda 14333$. In 3D geometry with $\sim 25\%$ mass in low-lanthanide regions ($X_{\mathrm{lan}} < 10^{-3}$), optical flux at $4500\text{--}5500\,\text{\AA}$ is reproduced without an independent lanthanide-free component. In contrast, 2D azimuthally averaged models mix lanthanides into polar sightlines, reducing $1\,\mathrm{d}$ luminosity threefold and producing an excessively red spectrum. Furthermore, standard expansion opacity overestimates uncollided packet transmission $P_0 = e^{-\tau_{\mathrm{bin}}} \approx e^{-1} \approx 0.37$ for optically thick lines ($\tau_l \gg 1$), overestimating early spectral flux by $10\%\text{--}20\%$.
analysis.problem: Previous 3D dynamical ejecta models possessed insufficient mass ($M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 0.005\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) and excessively high velocities relative to empirical inferences for AT2017gfo ($M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 0.03\text{--}0.05\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$), leaving unresolved whether early blue and optical emissions require an independent, distinct lanthanide-poor ejecta component and whether common 2D azimuthal averaging and expansion opacity approximations distort inferred physical properties.
analysis.method: Simulations utilize the 3D time-dependent Monte Carlo radiative transfer code ARTIS with homologous expansion ($r = v_r t$) mapped from a $2 \times 1.35\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ SPH binary neutron star merger snapshot at $t_{\mathrm{snap}} = 0.1\,\mathrm{d}$. Nuclear heating solves the Bateman equations for $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $^{254}\mathrm{Cf}$ fission, tracking non-instantaneous density-dependent charged particle thermalization and $\gamma$-ray transport. Ionization and excitation are treated in LTE via Saha-Boltzmann equations at local electron temperature $T_e$. Calculations employ the AD3 dataset containing $\approx 4.9 \times 10^7$ bound-bound transitions across 323 ions of 83 elements with wavelength-calibrated lanthanide levels. Radiative transfer benchmarks line-by-line (LBL) macroatom treatments against capped line-binned opacities with optical depth $\tau_{\mathrm{bin}} = \sum_i \min(\tau_i, \tau_{\mathrm{l,max}})$ and expansion opacities $\tau_{\mathrm{bin}} = \sum_i (1 - e^{-\tau_i})$.
assumptions: Homologous expansion ($r = v_r t$, $V \propto v_r^3$) from $t_{\mathrm{snap}} = 0.1\,\mathrm{d}$ onward.
limits: Velocity compression is an ad-hoc phenomenological scaling to mimic slower post-merger disk outflows rather than a self-consistent hydrodynamic simulation.

2.2 Atomic data: “In total, our AD3 atomic dataset contains about 49 million bound–bound transitions across 323 ionisation stages”
2.4.2 Transport across one bin: “expansion opacity can overestimate $P_{0}$ for a packet that traverses a wavelength bin with optically thick lines”
5.3 Implications for inferred ejecta properties: “Our velocity compression is a substitute for the slower post-merger ejecta that the model lacks”

analysis.research_progress: Establishes that combining mass scaling ($M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 0.04\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) with velocity compression ($v_r \lesssim 0.09c$) and 3D clumpy geometry self-consistently accounts for both early blue/optical emission and late infrared features without invoking an independent lanthanide-poor ejecta component; quantitatively proves that 2D azimuthal averaging causes artificial lanthanide mixing that suppresses $1\,\mathrm{d}$ flux by a factor of 3; and demonstrates that capped line-binned opacity with $\tau_{\mathrm{l,max}} \ge 5$ resolves the $10\%\text{--}20\%$ flux overestimate inherent to standard expansion opacity formulations.

figures.caption: Figure 8: Temperature versus mass density for the cells of the dyn 8x mass v/2 model in 3D (top) and in 2D on the $25{\times}50$ grid (bottom), for timesteps spanning 1.2–1.7 days. analysis.reason: This paper presents detailed NICER timing and time-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the brightest thermonuclear burst in the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658, providing critical observational constraints on burst-disc interaction and accretion physics in compact objects.
analysis.result: Using simultaneous reflection and persistent emission scaling (Model C), the burst peak exhibits an increased persistent scaling factor $f_{a,1}=59.6\pm 0.6$ and sub-unity reflection fractions $f_{r,1}=0.82\pm 0.15$ and $f_{r,2}=0.55\pm 0.06$. The direct burst bolometric luminosity peaks at $L_{\rm bol} \approx 0.68\,L_{\rm Edd}$, below the Eddington limit despite PRE characteristics. In the burst tail ($>200\,\mathrm{s}$), the absorption column density increases by $\approx 34\%$ ($N_{\mathrm{H}} = (2.42^{+0.13}_{-0.10})\times 10^{21}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$) and the accretion disc temperature increases by $\approx 15\%$ ($kT_{\mathrm{disc}} = 0.78^{+0.04}_{-0.03}\,\mathrm{keV}$), confirming burst-induced disc heating and geometric puffing.

analysis.problem: Investigating the physical origin of the soft X-ray excess ($<1.5\,\mathrm{keV}$) during super-bright thermonuclear bursts, the thermodynamic and structural impact of burst irradiation on the accretion disc, and whether persistent accretion emission evolves during the burst.
analysis.method: Performed energy-resolved light curve analysis and time-resolved X-ray spectroscopy ($0.5-10\,\mathrm{keV}$) using NICER. Tested three spectral configurations: variable disc blackbody (Model A, $\mathrm{tbabs} \times (\mathrm{bbodyrad} + \mathrm{diskbb} + \mathrm{nthcomp} + \mathrm{gauss})$), relativistic reflection (Model B, with $\mathrm{rdblur} \times \mathrm{bbrefl}$), and simultaneous reflection plus persistent emission scaling (Model C, combining reflection with the $f_a$-method where $F_{\rm pers} = f_a F_{\rm pers,0}$), extended into the burst tail ($>200\,\mathrm{s}$) and pre-burst phase.
assumptions: Iron abundance $A_{\rm Fe}$ can be tied across burst peak spectra.
